question: Which of the following best describes the difference between how energy and matter move through an ecosystem?
A: Energy flows in one direction and is eventually lost as heat, while matter is recycled among biotic and abiotic components
B: Both energy and matter cycle repeatedly through an ecosystem without being lost
C: Energy is recycled among trophic levels, while matter flows in one direction and leaves the ecosystem
D: Both energy and matter flow in a single direction and are lost from the ecosystem after one pass

stimulus.title: Fate of Energy vs. Matter in an Ecosystem
rows: Cycles among biotic and abiotic pools

question: A biome is best defined as a large geographic region characterized primarily by which of the following?
A: Its characteristic climate (temperature and precipitation patterns) and the resulting dominant vegetation and animal communities
B: The specific set of individual species present, regardless of climate
C: Its political boundaries and the human land-use activities that occur there
D: The single limiting nutrient that controls productivity in that region

question: A biologist samples a desert biome and a tropical rainforest biome to compare annual precipitation and mean temperature. Based on typical biome classifications, which combination of climate values would most likely describe the desert site compared to the rainforest site?
A: Much lower annual precipitation and greater daily temperature fluctuation than the rainforest
B: Higher annual precipitation and less daily temperature fluctuation than the rainforest
C: Similar annual precipitation but colder average annual temperature than the rainforest
D: Similar precipitation and similar temperature fluctuation to the rainforest

stimulus.title: Approximate Climate Data for Two Biomes

question: Which aquatic zone in a lake receives the most sunlight and supports the highest rate of photosynthesis?
A: The photic (limnetic) zone

C: The benthic zone
D: The abyssal zone

question: An estuary is best described as a transitional ecosystem where which of the following occurs?
A: Freshwater from rivers mixes with saltwater from the ocean, creating a brackish, highly productive habitat
B: Only freshwater organisms can survive due to the complete absence of salt
C: Water salinity remains constant and equal to open ocean salinity year-round
D: Photosynthesis is impossible due to consistently turbid, light-blocked water

question: In the carbon cycle, which process directly returns carbon dioxide from living organisms to the atmosphere?
A: Cellular respiration
B: Photosynthesis
C: Sedimentation
D: Nitrogen fixation

question: Which of the following processes converts atmospheric nitrogen gas (N2) into a form usable by plants?

D: Assimilation by plant roots

question: Farmers in a river valley apply nitrogen fertilizer to their fields each spring. Runoff data collected downstream over four years show a rise in nitrate concentration and a corresponding decline in dissolved oxygen during summer months. Which sequence of nitrogen-cycle processes best explains the observed decline in dissolved oxygen?
A: Excess nitrate stimulates algal growth; when algae die, bacterial decomposition of the biomass consumes dissolved oxygen
B: Nitrate is directly toxic to the bacteria that normally produce oxygen in the river, halting oxygen production
C: Denitrification converts nitrate into oxygen gas, which then escapes to the atmosphere and lowers dissolved oxygen
D: Nitrogen fixation consumes dissolved oxygen directly as bacteria convert nitrate into ammonia

stimulus.title: Downstream Nitrate and Dissolved Oxygen, Four-Year Trend

question: Unlike the carbon and nitrogen cycles, the phosphorus cycle has no significant atmospheric gas phase. Which of the following best explains why phosphorus moves so slowly through ecosystems compared to carbon or nitrogen?
A: Phosphorus is released mainly through the slow weathering of phosphate-containing rock, rather than through fast atmospheric exchange
B: Phosphorus is highly volatile and evaporates quickly from soil into the atmosphere before plants can use it
C: Phosphorus is consumed entirely by decomposers before it can re-enter the soil or water
D: Phosphorus exists only in living organisms and has no abiotic reservoirs at all

question: A lake receives phosphorus-laden runoff from surrounding farmland for many years. Researchers record the following changes in the lake over that time. Which explanation best accounts for the trend shown?
A: Excess phosphorus input is driving cultural eutrophication, fueling algal growth that depletes dissolved oxygen as it decomposes
B: The rising phosphorus levels are unrelated to the algal bloom, which is instead caused by increasing water temperature alone
C: Declining dissolved oxygen is causing the phosphorus level to rise, reversing the normal cause-and-effect relationship
D: Phosphorus and dissolved oxygen levels shown are within the range of normal, undisturbed lake variability

stimulus.title: Lake Water Quality Over a 20-Year Period

question: Which of the following best describes the role of transpiration in the hydrologic cycle?
A: The release of water vapor from plant leaves into the atmosphere
B: The downward movement of water through soil into groundwater
C: The condensation of water vapor into clouds
D: The direct runoff of precipitation into rivers and streams

stimulus.title: Hydrologic Cycle Processes
rows: Liquid water at a surface becomes water vapor
Water vapor released from plant leaves
Water moves into soil and groundwater

question: A watershed is deforested for agriculture. Hydrologists predict this will increase the volume and speed of surface runoff during storms compared to the forested condition. Which mechanism best explains this prediction?
A: Removing tree canopy and root systems reduces interception and infiltration, so more precipitation flows overland rather than soaking into the soil
B: Deforestation increases the rate of transpiration, which directly increases surface runoff during storms
C: Removing trees increases the soil's water-holding capacity, causing water to pool and then run off rapidly
D: Deforestation has no effect on runoff because precipitation amounts are determined only by atmospheric conditions

question: A food web, as opposed to a simple food chain, is best described as which of the following?

B: Primary producer
C: Decomposer
D: Detritivore

question: A researcher removes the top predator from a small experimental pond food web and monitors the abundance of species at each trophic level over the following two years. Populations of the predator's prey (mid-level consumers) increase sharply, while populations of the prey's food source (primary producers) decline sharply. This pattern best illustrates which ecological concept?
A: A trophic cascade, in which the effects of removing a top predator propagate down through multiple trophic levels
B: Primary succession, in which a community develops on newly exposed substrate with no prior soil
C: The 10% rule, which describes energy loss between trophic levels but not population-level effects of predator removal
D: Resource partitioning, in which competing species divide a limited resource to reduce competition
